source: one full verify of the privileged reference (solution/ as committed) under ale validate in the separate-verifier layout on an 8-CPU, 64 GB sandbox (2026-11-07): mean AP 72.339 over the 448 hidden frames, ap_gain 64.4729, 448 of 448 frames valid, 0 timeouts, slowest call 94.5 s of its 300 s limit. Its work per frame is fixed (no clock). Since 2026-11-14 the OpenBLAS kernels are pinned to Haswell (OPENBLAS_CORETYPE: the image, the solver processes and the scoring; tests/numerics_check.py refuses to grade otherwise), because the OpenBLAS 0.3.20 inside numpy 1.23.5 picks its kernels by CPU and the ones it picks on Intel CPUs with AVX512_BF16 return wrong matrix products: there the reference stayed below this anchor (mean AP 63.5 in a collaborator's run on a Xeon Platinum 8490H) and the scoring itself was wrong. The pin does not move the anchor: on 28 hidden frames the reference's output is bit-identical under the Haswell, SkylakeX and Zen kernels and under the kernels the anchor machine's CPU selects (emulated), and the starting detector gives baseline_mean_ap to the last digit on all 448 frames. What still differs between machines is numpy's own float64 sin and cos, which take an AVX-512 path where the CPU has one and change the reference's candidates in the last bit: between two hosts (16 frames, 2026-11-07) its AP differed by at most 2.0 per frame and by -0.31 on their mean, about 0.5 % of the gain, and switching numpy's AVX-512 paths off reproduces a difference of that size (7 frames: at most 2.0 per frame, +0.16 on their mean), while the score of a given array did not change (7 frames); full_at 0.98 covers that.
reference_commit: solution/ of the 2026-11-07 maintainer fixes (the commit that set this anchor)
note: ap_gain = max(0, mean AP - baseline_mean_ap) over the 448 hidden frames; baseline_mean_ap is the starting detector's mean AP, re-measured with this grader (7.866108398398201, identical). Reference = solution/: grasplib candidates ranked by a gradient-boosted scorer; with the ground truth that the grader exports only to a submission carrying the oracle token (tests/verify.py privileged()), the best 8000 candidates are checked for collision and emptiness and, per object, up to 40 of the survivors (after the evaluator's NMS) get graspnetAPI's own force-closure test; the output is sorted by that true label.
